discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can drive a time-reversal-invariant insulator into a new topological phase, the quantum spin Hall state, characterised by a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states. This identified an entirely new class of topological matter beyond the quantum Hall effect, later generalised to three-dimensional topological insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp and collaborators realised this phase in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, observing quantised edge conductance independent of sample width, an unambiguous transport signature, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Together these works created the field of topological insulators and superconductors, including the Fu-Kane route to Majorana bound states, higher-order topological phases, and the wide search for topologically protected quantum information. It is an exemplary interplay of clean theory, a concrete materials proposal, and decisive experiment.
